Albin has recently risen to significance during the Alphonso administration as an aggressive debater and a strong supporter of Ewald Alphonso and his policies. He was instrumental in the passing of the free market reforms of Alphonso. He became famed for his controversial speeches in the Grand National Assembly, and was labelled as the face of “a new generation” of the USP by the media.

After the recession, he joined the calls for a congress to elect a new presidential nominee and abandoned his support to Ewald Alphonso. Albin nominated himself as the next candidate but did not get much support in the congress, which eventually led to the candidacy of Anton Rayne.

In 1956, President Rayne appointed Albin Clavin as the vice president.

Gloria Tory is a Sordish politician and jurist who currently serves as a Justice of the Supreme Court of Sordland. She previously served as the Speaker of the Grand National Assembly of Sordland and as a member of the assembly.

After graduating from Holsord State University, Gloria was elected as the president of the student organization, Republican Youth. She supported the democratic revolutionaries and was credited for organizing several major student rallies during the last years of the Sordish monarchy.

Before her election to the assembly, she worked at several jobs, including a lobbying firm and a school of public speaking and debating. In 1929, she became a member of the United Sordland National Committee from Vesord.

Gloria rose quickly in USP after she was elected to the Grand National Assembly in 1937. She was appointed as a special adviser to the Minister of Interior in 1938, before being brought as the frontbench spokeswoman for Home Affairs in 1942, and the spokeswoman for Education in 1944. In 1949, she was elected as the Speaker of the Grand National Assembly, in protest against President Ewald Alphonso's reformist agenda. She is the first woman in Sordland to hold that position.

She was a strong critic of Ewald Alphonso’s presidency, and she became famed for her obstructions in the assembly of some of his policies. Regarded as a charismatic politician and a tough negotiator, she is credited for major lobbying incidents within the USP which shifted the political landscape during the last decade. After the 1953 elections, she was elected speaker for a second time.

In 1956, President Rayne appointed Gloria Tory to the Supreme Court.

Katarina Horten is a Sordish labour leader, politician and activist of Bludish descent, member of the assembly and the current spokesperson of the Labour Union of Sordland.

Born in Deyr, Bergia, to a Sordish Bludish family, Horten began her working life as a manual laborer before studying law at the Holsord State University. Relocating to Holsord, where she married, she got involved in the Sordland headquarters of the Watchtower of Human Rights (WHR), through which she helped laborers register to vote.

In 1942, she became the WHR's Sordland director. Later in 1948, she left the WHR to join the Labour Union of Sordland through which she launched an insurance scheme and a local newspaper for Bergian farmworkers. She began organizing strikes among farmworkers, some of which had been successful. Horten is known for her emphasis on direct but nonviolent tactics to pressure the state and the farm owners into granting the demands of the strikers. Receiving much support from labor and leftist groups, she was appointed as the spokesperson of the Labour Union of Sordland in 1950.

In the 1953 elections, she ran as an independent and was elected to be a member of the assembly.

As a staunch anti-Sollist, she was behind the organization of several major protests against Tarquin Soll in the 1940’s. She later became renowned for her support for the Agno-Sordish and Bludish minorities. Mansoun Leke is a Sordish politician of Bludish descent, member of the assembly and the current leader of the independents in the Grand National Assembly of Sordland. He was the leader of the pro-Bludish Workers Party of Bludia between 1948 and 1949. He is a strong advocate for the rights of religious and ethnic minorities.

During his education in Holsord State University in the Department of Literature in 1925, he faced political problems due to his Bludish background and his left-leaning views, which forced him to leave school without finishing his degree. He later enrolled in Deyr University of Culture and graduated with a degree in Merkopan History.

After the Izzam Incident in 1933, and the ban on the Bludish Freedom Party, he returned to his hometown in Uziren and campaigned to organize the Bludish minority under a new democratic political movement. He was allegedly invited to join the militant Bludish Freedom Front by Dewlen Arge personally. He heavily protested against Arge’s call for a full-scale insurgency in the region of Bergia, arguing that ‘violence would only result in more violence’.

In 1948, he joined the Workers Party of Bludia. The same year, he was elected to be the leader of the party and ran as a presidential candidate in the 1949 elections. He coined the slogan, ‘peace in Bludia, peace in Sordland, peace in the world.’

In the ‘49 elections, he got 6% of the general vote, failing to pass the election threshold. He later resigned from his position despite protests from his own party and ran as an independent in the 1953 elections to bypass the threshold. He was elected as a Member of Assembly in 1953.

Remus Holstron is a Sordish politician, member of Assembly, the founding member of the National Front Party (NFP), and its current leader. He has been serving in the Grand National Assembly of Sordland since 1937. He is nicknamed ‘the Iron Wall’ by the NFP supporters. He was elected to lead the NFP in 1957.

He is believed to have been active within the organization during the Sordish Civil War. He was blamed by the Bludish Freedom Party and the Communist Party of Sordland for having been behind many of the atrocities that took place against the Bludish and the communists between 1927 to 1930. He has denied such claims and holds no official membership position in the Young Sords.

As a founding member of the NFP, he promoted ethnonationalist policies in the 1930’s and became a famous figure for his aggressive speeches in the Grand National Assembly. Kibener heavily protested against his political stance, saying that ‘Mr. Holstron and many others in our leadership created an unapproachable and unreasonable political movement which is expected to lose in every election.’

With the rise of Kesaro Kibener in the 1940’s, he lost his influence in the party and resigned in 1949 after Kibener was voted in as the leader. He was later invited by Kibener to rejoin the party ahead of the 1953 elections and was appointed as the party’s Group Deputy Chairman.

In 1957, he was elected as the leader of the NFP.

Marcel Koronti is a Sordish businessman, philanthropist, entrepreneur who is the son of the famous media proprietor Konrath Koronti. He is currently being held in Antel Rock Prison. He transformed HOS Resorts from a leading hotel chain in Sordland into an international powerhouse through his expansion of the brand into 7 different countries.

In 1950, he left HOS Resorts and started operating the HOS Advertising, the advertising company within the HOS Media Group of the HOS conglomerate.

Gus Manger is a politician and businessman who serves as the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development in the Rayne administration. Gus Manger has been a United Sordland Party member since 1933 and served as the Minister of Development under the Alphonso government. He is the only cabinet member who managed to retain a ministerial position from the Alphonso administration.

Gus was born in Valgen in 1899 to a family of old landowners who cultivated many farms in the Gruni region and exported crops, fruits, and other products to Lespia. He studied business at the University of Valgen, and later worked with OMEC in 1931 to help develop local agricultural, logistical, and energy companies. Manger used his OMEC connections to help Gasom, a company that contracted him, to attract top engineering talent.

After helping his home region find foreign direct investment, he diversified his investments. Gus saw great potential in Anrica, as a middle-ground between the most prominent cities. He made significant investments there in the early 1940s, founding and running a successful logistics and tourism company. His strong relations with the city led him to acquire minority ownership in FC Anrica, the city's football club.

In 1943 he was appointed deputy to the Minister of Economy, Commerce, and Energy of Tarquin Soll's 4th cabinet. After the party congress of 1946 and the loss of party leadership of Tarquin Soll, Gus joined the Alphonso government as Minister of Development. Gus was particularly successful in helping rural poverty reduction through international investment attraction, arranging high-value export routes for locally produced agricultural goods, and adjusting import and export taxes to drive the generated economic value up in Sordland. 

Between 1950 and 1952, he was crucial in arranging landmark trade deals with countries like Rizia, Lespia, and Anraka to improve the trade deficit of Sordland and help the economy to stabilize. Manger worked tirelessly during and after the 51 recession with the "Three Econs," consisting of Edith Agnoc, Mikail Aven, and Symon Holl, and helped Sordland avoid economic depression.

He eventually supported Anton Rayne in 1953 after the collapse of the Alphonso cabinet. He was given the adjusted position of Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development in the Rayne administration in 1954. 

He sold his shares in Gasom and departed from the company.

He has been a member of the United Sordland Party since its formation in 1929. Prior to his position as minister, he held the position of Inspector General of the Army, serving directly under the Chief of Staff of the Sordish Army.

He was a captain during the Sordland Civil War and served under the command of Colonel Tarquin Soll before his presidency. He gained nation-wide fame after his heroism and accomplishments as major during the Wehlen Civil War, which also earned him the highest military order.

Iosef became a popular figure after the wars, and still is well respected among the nationalists. He is credited for several major military operations and known to be an influential figure in the Sordish Armed Forces. He has been promoting the reformation of the army into a professional rather than a conscripted force.

He was a big critic of Ewald Alphonso’s policies. He gave his support to Anton Rayne and lobbied for major conservative support in the 1953 elections for the USP. He was appointed by the General Staff as the Minister of Defense and Security. In 1956, he assumed the role of the chief of the Sordish Armed Forces after the dismissal of Valken Kruger, and was later elected as the chief of the Sordish General Staff.

Lileas Graf is a Sordish politician who has served as the current Minister of Interior of Sordland from 1953 until her arrest in 1957. Then, she served as the mayor of Arvory from 1940 to 1947, and the mayor of Holsord from 1948 to 1952.

Lileas started her political career as an elected official on Arvory City Council. Her tenure as public advocate saw a reformation of various housing, finance and security policies. Then, she was elected mayor of Arvory in 1940 and her accomplishments in the city brought her nationwide popularity. This prompted Tarquin Soll to pick her to replace the mayor of Holsord. Her policies on urban planning and public education transformed Holsord’s economy and boosted her popularity in the capital. She is currently one of the central figures in the United Sordland party.

Lileas is credited for the economic booms in both Arvory and Holsord, and known for supporting socially conservative politics throughout her career. She is respected as an expert on urban development and police relations. As one of the most influential supporters of Anton Rayne’s candidacy in 1953 elections, she inarguably brought with her a large conservative support. Soon after, she left her position as the mayor of Holsord to become a minister under the Rayne administration.

In 1957, Lileas was dismissed from her post as minister and arrested under charges of treason. She is being held in Antel Rock prison.

Galade's academic background is in sociology and law. He studied sociology at Kingshill University before pursuing law at Imperial Markian University. He completed these demanding courses of study in an unusually short period of time, from 1917 to 1920. A gap exists in the public record of Galade's activities for about a decade following his graduation.

Galade's career reemerges in the public record in the 1930s when he worked as a lawyer and chief strategy officer at multiple think tanks and public relations agencies in Lachaven. He transitioned into politics in the early 1930s, providing legal counsel to several influential assembly members in Holsord. He also served as the spokesperson for the United Sordland National Committee during the second and third terms of Soll's presidency. Additionally, Galade was an advisor to the Interior Minister during Tarquin Soll's final presidential term in the 1940s.

Galade is recognized in political circles for his strategic acumen, and his role in recent electoral successes has further enhanced his reputation. While his contributions often go unnoticed by the public, he is highly regarded within the cabinet for his extensive experience and expertise in law and media.

Galade was one of the earliest supporters of Anton Rayne's presidential candidacy in 1953. His strategic input was crucial to the success of Rayne's election campaign. Following Rayne's victory, Galade took on his current role as the president's chief strategist, a position which solidifies his influence in Sordish politics.

In 1956, Galade was appointed as Vice President by President Rayne, due to his political acumen and influence. This marked a significant milestone in his political career.

Nia was a strong critic of Tarquin Soll’s programs and vocal about her opposition to the Supreme Court’s authority on state matters. Due to her expertise on Sordish law, she was appointed by Ewald Alphonso as the Vice Minister of Law in 1949.

She earned her reputation from her fight against corruption in the ministry among protests from the Supreme Court. She is regarded as one of the most experienced attorneys who worked for the government. She eventually gave her support to Anton Rayne and was appointed as the Minister of Justice and Law in 1953.

In 1957, Nia resigned from her position as minister due to disagreements with President Rayne.

Alma Saltana is the current Prime Minister of the Republic of Morella and the leader of the left-wing coalition Morellan Unified Front.

Born into a Qinali-Morellan family of modest means in the capital city of Cavette, she developed a passion for politics and activism at an early age. During university, she completed a year abroad at the People's University of United Contana; the Malenyevist teachings she was exposed to there informed her later work as a labor lawyer and community organizer.

She eventually joined the Morellan Social Democrat party, where she quickly rose to the rank of vice-chairwoman. Seizing the opportunity presented by the economic crisis of the 1940s, she successfully united the country's left-leaning parties to form the Morellan Unified Front coalition, which replaced Morella's right-wing, authoritarian government in 1950. 

As a PM, she has enacted significant social reforms, emphasizing the importance of the redistribution of wealth and the role of the state in providing for the welfare of all citizens. However, her political rivals have criticized the speed with which these changes were implemented and their potential for alienating Morella's international allies.

Grand Duke Axel Reinhart is the ruler of the Grand Duchy of Pales. He is the youngest scion of the Reinhart family, who have ruled the Grand Duchy since the conclusion of the War of Rizian Succession in 1810. As the younger brother of Duke Njolma, he was groomed from a young age to succeed the throne, receiving an education in Palesian, Rizian and Valgish from a cadre of elite tutors and prestigious institutions.

Growing up, he was often featured in the international tabloids for his good looks and variety of interests. He has displayed a penchant for equestrian sports, classical music, and archaeological exploration, and his pursuits have often been marked by a blend of thrill and scholarly curiosity. 

His charisma made him a popular figure among the Palesian and Rizian speakers of Pales alike, and following his brother Njolma's abdication in 1948, he was a natural choice for successor.

Beatrice Livingston, born in 1905, is the Queen of the Kingdom of Rumburg and the proclaimed ruler of All of Northern Merkopa. She acceded to the throne in November 1921 at the age of sixteen following the death of her father, King Alfred II. Under Rumburg's Regency Act, she reigned in her minority until eighteen, with executive authority exercised by a regency headed by Regent Duke Eadric Wulfsbury.

The opening phase of her reign coincided with the War of Broken Wills (1921–1924), which began under the regency and ended with the Treaty of Konstantium, co-signed by Beatrice alongside Lord Chancellor Godric Falkenridge. The war and its outcome became one of the defining political victories of her reign, consolidating her authority and shaping her reputation as a ruler capable of advancing Rumburgian interests through both military and diplomatic channels.

After assuming full authority, she reigned as a constitutional monarch through major political changes, including centralization measures, secularization reforms, and the dissolution and integration of northern territories into the kingdom. In 1926, Rumburg aided Rizia with supplies during the Uprising after King Valero requested assistance. In domestic politics she initially aligned with the Crown Preservation Party, while maintaining differences on religious policy, a conflict that culminated in a political break in 1928. After the rupture she recalibrated her governing alliances, building new court and parliamentary partnerships, with her later internal security agenda and external posture more often associated with GRUP-backed arguments for forward frontier influence.

Shaped by the costly wars of the previous century that slowed Rumburg's advance and strained its institutions, Beatrice is often described as preferring legal and diplomatic solutions where possible, while treating force as a last resort when other channels failed. In foreign policy, the Queen codified her approach as the Beatrice Doctrine, presented under the title "The Great Unification," framed in royal messaging as the survival and growth of monarchies after the Century of Revolutions. Following the socialist revolution in Valgsland, she cancelled Alfred II's plans for an Eastern Merkopan Pact with Valgsland and instead pursued closer commercial ties with Arcasia through major trade deals, while also advancing GRACE as Rumburg's primary framework for coordination among aligned monarchies. 

In 1932, she supported closer ties with Rizia and helped arrange the marriage of her sister, Princess Lena Livingston, to Prince Romus Toras (later King Romus Toras), a union that formalized a dynastic link between the two royal houses. Beatrice gained infamy for selling weapons to both the attackers and defenders during the Wehlen Civil War, and despite official denials, Rumburg is widely believed to have been heavily involved in both the Wehlen Civil War and the Sordish Civil War, drawing sharp criticism from United Contana and diplomatic friction with Arcasia.

Court politics became more prominent in the late 1930s and 1940s, including an intensified use of Livingston and allied noble marriages into GRUP-aligned circles as part of broader bloc management and elite consolidation. By the 1950s, Rumburg's policy under the Queen was increasingly shaped by industrial resource demands and raw material supply concerns alongside its external commitments. She has periodically faced republican sentiment and criticism of the royal family, particularly in response to reforms viewed as reducing the practical authority of the Parliament of Rumburg.

Jorga Azmal is the Supreme Wiseman of Derdian Golcondism, and therefore the leader of the Nurist Republic of Derdia.

Azmal grew up within the Golcondist community of Outer Neael, where he achieved the rank of Adept at just 16 years old. He studied Wruhecist philosophy at Neael University before becoming a disciple of Rasma Atafor, Derdia's first Supreme Wiseman. In the early 1940s, he published a book based on Atafor's teachings that was widely distributed to schools and households across the country. When Atafor died in 1945, Azmal was unanimously voted in as his successor.

Azmal has mostly continued the strict religion-based policies of his predecessor; the only notable departure has been his focus on weapons programs as a "necessary step towards achieving Golconda". He lives in a heavily guarded compound built into the mountains above Neael, which he runs as a self-sustaining Golcondist community, disconnected from the city's water and energy grid.

Leon "Malenyev" Chavatangakwunua is a Contanan revolutionary, politician, and political theorist who has been serving as the head of government of United Contana since 1910. He is the architect of Malenyevism, a unique variant of Marcian socio-economics. Chavatangakwunua played a significant role in transforming Kontania, and subsequently United Contana, into a communist state governed by the Contanan Communist Party.

Born into a poor family in the Kontanian Empire (now part of United Contana), Chavatangakwunua was drawn to revolutionary socialist politics following his brother's execution. He relocated to Kyow in 1901, where he became a senior theorist of Marcian Socio-economics. Inspired by Karlos Marcia's political theory, Chavatangakwunua developed Malenyevism upon joining the Marcianist Contanan Labour Party.

Chavatangakwunua was instrumental in the party's ideological split, leading the Rotski faction against other factions and promoting Malenyevism within the party. He advocated for the transformation of the Century of Revolutions into a Contana-wide proletarian revolution, which he believed would result in the overthrow of capitalism and its replacement with socialism. Chavatangakwunua led the Rotskis during the 1907 Revolution, ultimately declaring a communist republic and deposing the King.

Under Chavatangakwunua's leadership, United Contana underwent rapid industrialization and collectivization through the implementation of a command economy and the pursuit of socialist reforms. This strategy led to the development and modernization of the entire continent. Chavatangakwunua's ideology has been adapted and interpreted into different schools of thought worldwide, with the number of Marco-Malenyevists steadily increasing, cementing his position as one of the most influential leaders of the century.

Chavatangakwunua is particularly renowned for his massive education and science plan, which has elevated United Contana to a position of technological supremacy in the region, rivaling Arcasia. Through his commitment to educational reforms and investment in scientific research, United Contana has emerged as a powerhouse in technological innovation, driving economic growth and solidifying its status as a global superpower.

Romus Toras was born in 1905 in the Kingdom of Rizia, Valenqiris. He is the only child of the late king Valero "The Frail" Toras and Queen Mother Estela Toras, and holds the title of King of Rizia as well as the symbolic title of Duke of Valenqiris. 

Following the death of Queen Lyza in 1918, his father Valero ascended to the throne, a period marked by political uncertainty and rumors of unrest. Romus received his education in Porte Drazon, where he was largely isolated from commoner life.

Shortly after the prince's coming of age, Rizia entered into a conflict with the newly independent Grand Duchy of Pales that eventually escalated into a nationwide crisis, culminating in Romus's capture by insurgents led by Lucas Sazon, Duke of Brenas. His subsequent rescue by Wehzek forces marked a critical juncture in Rizian politics. The aftermath of the revolt saw significant changes, including the leasing of Zille to Wehlen and the execution of Lucas Sazon, with Romus assuming governance of Valenqiris.

Romus' tenure as Duke was marked by significant events including his strategic marriage to Lena Livingston, sister of Queen Beatrice of Rumburg. Following his wife's death in a tragic sailing accident in 1942, he became the sole guardian of their child, Princess Vina Toras.

Romus' ascension to the throne followed the death of his father in 1949, marking the beginning of his reign as King of Rizia.

Ewald Alphonso is a statesman, businessman and politician, who served as the third President of Sordland from 1949 to 1953. He was the leader of the United Sordland Party from 1946 to 1953. He is particularly famed for winning against Tarquin Soll in the ‘46 Congress, bringing an end to Soll’s domination of the USP.

After studying civil engineering at Kingshill University, he briefly worked in the state department for oil and gas planning in 1924. He later undertook postgraduate studies on energy planning and management in Arcasia between 1927 and 1929. He returned to Sordland after the end of the Sordish Civil War and started working for the Gasom Corporation. He bought a large portion of the shares of the company after Contanan partners pulled out, and was later elected as its CEO.

During the construction of the Soll Dam, he worked as a project advisor and in 1935 was appointed Head of the Department of Energy, under the Ministry of Economy. He joined the USP in 1940 and was elected to the executive committee of the USP in 1941.

Alphonso gained a huge following in a very short time after his campaigns for free market reforms, and in 1946 ran as a candidate for party leadership against Tarquin Soll. He won the ‘46 congress and became the chairman of the USP. President Soll appointed him as Vice President and he came the de-facto government leader as the President stepped back from politics. He later ran as a presidential candidate in the general elections of 1949 and was elected president. He was supported by influential figures like Kris Schar, Konrath Koronti and Walter Tusk, which are believed to have played a great role in his election as president.

His term saw many market reforms that were implemented very quickly in his first year. He privatized several industries, brought tax cuts, relaxed immigration policies and changed several of Tarquin Soll’s authoritarian laws to bring foreign investment to Sordland. However, he was faced with the economic recession of 1951, which quickly proved to be the worst economic crisis in Sordland since the Sordish Civil War. Some claim the ineffectiveness of his economic reforms were the result of a conspiracy by the Old Guard.

In 1953, his cabinet resigned after his inability to control the economic crisis. He resigned from politics after losing the party congress against Anton Rayne. Upon his departure from politics, Alphonso channeled his leadership and resources towards philanthropic efforts, establishing the Alphonso Foundation. The foundation dedicates its mission to alleviating homelessness and actively engaging in philanthropic initiatives aimed at bridging income inequality gaps.

He faded into obscurity following the bankruptcy and closure of Gasom.

Tarquin Soll (Colonel Soll) is a military officer and politician, who served as the 2nd President of Sordland between 1929 and 1949. In 1957, he was charged with lifetime imprisonment for his crimes against the Sordish people. He is still regarded by some Sollists as the founder of the Republic of Sordland since the first years of the republic between 1923 and 1927 were short lived due to the Civil War.

Soll assumed the post in 1929 by ending the Sordish Civil War and taking control of the government under military rule. He is the founder of the United Sordland Party. He is regarded as the most significant and controversial person in Sordland’s history.

Tarquin was a colonel and the commander of the 6th army of the Sordish Armed Forces when General Luderin executed a military coup in 1927, which he did not join. Later in 1927, Civil War broke out between armies of the Sordish military as well as militant political organizations. Following this, Tarquin Soll and the 6th Army joined the war and managed to win several major battles against both General Luderin and General Rikard. In January 1929, the 6th army took control of Holsord and started pushing the rebels to the east. Later in the year, Tarquin Soll put an end to the Sordish Civil War, took control of the government, wrote a new Constitution, and called the Grand National Assembly back to work. He formed the USP and went to elections with one party and became the President of Sordland.

His first years saw many developments in Sordland, restoring and surpassing the pre-Civil War production levels. He invested heavily into infrastructure, healthcare and police forces. Many forgotten areas of Sordland were provided with services for the first time in their history during Soll administration. He also addressed the much problematic energy problem of Sordland with the Soll Dam project in Erzaren which triggered the 1933 Izzam Incident and a long conflict with Bludish separatists.

After his first term as President, Tarquin called for elections in 1933 and ran as a candidate in the first ever elections of Sordland with multiple parties, which still resulted in a massive win for Tarquin Soll and the USP. In total he won five elections and served as President of Sordland for twenty years.

His later terms saw further economic developments along with an increase in political and racial tensions in Sordland. Many Bludish activists and politicians were arrested, communists were detained for suspected crimes against the state. The media was under his control and censored the opposing voices. Many different political parties entered politics to oppose Tarquin Soll’s leadership, and several of them were closed down.

In the 1940’s, the opposition against Tarquin Soll reached new heights, triggering major protests against him within the USP. In the late 1940’s, the new reformist wing in the party saw a great increase in its influence and started to challenge Tarquin. In 1946, he lost the leadership vote to Ewald Alphonso and resigned as the chairman of the USP. He went on to serve as President of Sordland until 1949.

After his resignation as president, he moved to reside in Duru Island at the mouth of the Gulf of Nargis. He was the only person who held the title “Member of Honor” -- which gave him total immunity as well as an indefinite right to partake in the Grand National Assembly of Sordland -- before the amendments proposed by Anton Rayne removed his immunity from the constitution.

In 1957, he was put on trial for “crimes against Sordish people” by the wishes of President Rayne. The Supreme Court charged him with lifetime imprisonment. He is currently being held in Antel Rock Prison.

Alfred Kcirbuk is a Sordish film director, producer and screenwriter. He is one of the most influential Sordish directors of the decade, and the only Sordish director to ever be nominated for the prestigious Motion Picture Awards in Arcasia.

While in his twenties, Kcirbuk directed a number of stage productions for the state theaters, including an adaptation of the famous ‘Unger’ with an entirely Bludish cast. His first film was ‘Resident Karl,’ a controversial movie with socio political commentary on Sordland, which is consistently ranked the greatest Sordish film ever made. It was later banned in Sordland by Tarquin Soll in 1940.

By 1945, Kcirbuk was a filmmaker of international importance, with several of his films being screened in various other countries. He wrote and directed famous movies such as ‘Rebeka’, ‘A Touch of Satan’ and ‘Eyes Wide Open.’

In 1953, his film ‘The Sordish Dream’ was nominated for the best foreign film in the Arcasian Motion Picture Awards.

Dewlen Arge is a Bludish political leader, a founding member of the militant Bludish Freedom Front (BFF), who has been a political prisoner since his arrest in 1944. He used to be the leader of the BFF between 1935 and 1944. He is being held in the Antel Rock Prison.

According to some sources, Arge was born in a border village between Wehlen and Sordland. During his youth, he was a member of the Republican Youth and supported the revolution against the monarchy in the Kingdom of Sordland. After the fall of the monarchy, he joined the youth wing of the Bludish Freedom Party (BFP) to promote the improvement of the Bludish rights.

After the cancellation of the first ever elections in Sordland by General Luderin and the subsequent civil war in 1927, he wanted to fight against the military coup by joining the Sordish Armed Forces under the leadership of General Rikard, but was denied entry due to his ethnicity. This prompted him to return to Bergia to organize the Bludish populace to also join the civil war with their own militia army, but couldn’t gather a large support.

After the war, he started working in Erzaren as a simple merchant and serving in the local council of the Bludish Freedom Party. When he learned about the plans of the Soll Dam in 1933, he participated in the protests against the construction with other members of the BFP and experienced the Izzam Incident first-hand. After the death of Aschraf and the ban on the BFP, he fled to the village of Zensehir, and along with a group of students, formed an organization called ‘The Followers of Aschraf.’ They later changed their name to Bludish Freedom Front.

In 1935, Arge took control of the BFF and announced a full-scale Bludish uprising in the region of Bergia. He gained great infamy when his forces took control of Uziren and defended the town against the Sordish Armed Forces for two weeks. Between 1935 and 1944, he was behind many armed attacks against the Sordish military, Sordish police as well as civilians. He was finally arrested in 1944 and was imprisoned in Antel Rock Prison.

President Ephraim Nines is an economist and former diplomat who serves as the President of the Alliance of Nations. 

Born into poverty in Konstantium, Kyrute, President Nines struggled with literacy during his early education. Despite these obstacles, his aptitude for numbers stood out, and he eventually taught himself to read. It was only later in life that he discovered his struggles stemmed from undiagnosed dyslexia.

Nines graduated from the prestigious Konstantium University with a degree in Economics and International Relations, a rigorous hybrid program blending economics, political science, and international affairs. His academic achievements paved the way for his first major role as an Economic Development Specialist at the International Economic Development Authority (IEDA). The organization's mission is to foster global economic stability and support sustainable growth in developing nations.

Demonstrating exceptional skill and leadership, Nines rapidly rose through the agency ranks, ultimately becoming its director by age 35.

In 1937, the Kyrute government appointed Nines to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, where he served in various diplomatic roles. By 1941, he was selected as Kyrute's Permanent Representative to the Alliance of Nations, gaining invaluable experience in peacekeeping and international cooperation. His efforts culminated in his election as President of the Alliance of Nations in 1948.

President Nines is known for bringing a quiet but firm hand to diplomacy.

Giralt Haute-Bellasorde, or more commonly known as Giralt of Ribery, was a pioneering Sordish viticulturist and winemaker of Lespian descent, who was the first to cultivate the famous Borin grape. He is known as ‘the father of Sordish viticulture.’

Giralt of Ribery is credited with introducing important innovations to Sordish winemaking. He was born in Ribery. He began producing wine under his own label, Dandelion, in the 1910s. He was particularly known for the quality of his wines which used grapes from Borin and Erlory.

Dandelion wines are now highly sought after and renowned for their floral tones and elegance, as well as their lushness and concentration.

Ishval Ersen is a distinguished Bludish lawyer and civil rights activist who's based in Deyr, Sordland. Born in 1909 in Uziren, Ersen completed his legal education at Deyr University of Culture in 1932 and has since dedicated his career to addressing civil rights issues in Bergia and wider Sordland, advocating for the Bludish community.

Throughout his career, he has been unyielding in the face of adversity, including an eviction from his home under dubious charges of 'threatening public stability and safety.' Beyond his courtroom work, Ersen has engaged in political and social debates. Notably, he has critiqued certain government policies like the controversial Resettlement Order, voicing concerns over potential infringement on the rights of the Bludish people.

Ersen has also questioned the coherence of Sordland's Constitution, suggesting a possible conflict between Articles 6 and 7 and the rights defined in Article 100. The case he filed against Governor Bron rocketed him to nationwide fame.

Johan Gasmich is a Sordish communist revolutionary of Agno-Sordish descent, activist and the founder and leader of the Red Youth.

Gasmich studied in Arvory State School and later at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering of Lachaven Technical University. He initially supported President Artor Wisci and his national democratic movement, but later changed his view. After reading about Marcian socio-economics, he translated Karlos Marcia’s biography into Sordish.

Inspired by Marcian Socio-economics, Malenyevism and Valgslandian socialism, he founded and led the Socialist Students Association of Lachaven Technical University. In 1927, Gasmich founded the Red Youth and joined the armed resistance against General Luderin’s military takeover.

He admired the guerilla fighters in Rika who fought against colonisation and created a strategy of armed guerilla warfare to achieve what he called the people’s revolution. He is suspected to be the person who devised the plan to assassinate General Luderin in 1928 with a group of Red Youth revolutionaries. The attempt failed when Luderin’s soldiers confronted the group and all the activists were killed. He is suspected to be within the group, but managed to escape.

After the Sordish Civil War, Gasmich began his editorial career as the editor-in-chief for the Tussle magazine where he worked together with Denis Stahler. He continued his political life in the struggle for the unification of Sordland's socialist movement.

Tuomas Sacker, born 1912, is a Kyrutean journalist and television interviewer known for his work in both print and broadcast media. He began his career at the Konstantium Defender, where he rose to become a senior journalist and managing editor. Sacker studied political science and journalism at the University of Konstantium and gained early recognition for investigative reporting and his political contacts within Kyrute’s diplomatic and media circles.

Watani Aschraf was a Bludish carpenter who was killed by Sordish soldiers during his protest against the construction of the Soll Dam. His death and the subsequent chaos that escalated between the protesters and the Sordish soldiers came to be known as the Izzam Incident. He became a symbol of the Bludish resistance movement in Sordland.

Not much is known about Aschraf other than his work as a carpenter in the village of Izzam near Erzaren. According to many sources, he was respected as the village’s elder and many villagers seeked his advice. In 1933, when Sordish authorities came to the village to force the villagers out of their homes, he refused to leave his home. He took part in the protests against Soll Dam, which threatened to destroy Izzam by leaving it under water.

He was shot and killed by a soldier on the tenth day of the protests. Following his death, his name became a symbol of Bludish rights. His death is mourned by the Bludish democrats and the Bludish separatists alike. The Bludish Freedom Front was initially called ‘The Followers of Aschraf.’

Denis Stahler is a Sordish political theorist and politician who serves as the current leader of the Communist Party of Sordland (CPS.) Originally starting politics in the first Communist Party with the same name that existed between 1924 and 1928, he later joined People’s Freedom and Justice Party (PFJP,) and in 1950, co-founded the second Communist Party of Sordland in 1950.

Stahler became an exponent of communist ideas during his studies in the University of Haelm in Valgsland. After earning his doctorate in political economy, he moved to Holsord in 1927, where he hoped to open a lawyer’s office. He joined the Communist Party (1924-1928) and faced prosecution under General Luderin after the ban on the Communist Party in 1928. Fearing the complete annihilation of Sordish socialists by the junta, he moved to Valgsland and assisted the Red Youth by establishing connections between the Sordish and Valgslandian socialists with the help of the governing People’s Party of Valgsland.

After the civil war, he worked as a lawyer in Holsord, often defending other left-wing socialists. He was involved with smuggling Malenyevist propaganda from United Contana to Sordland as well as writing and publishing his own socialist magazine, ‘Tussle.’ He wrote extensively against militarism and authoritarianism. Because of his political theories on communism and physical resemblance to Emmerich Hegel, he was given the nickname ‘Sordish Hegel’ by his admirers.

Despite being regarded as a Malenyevist in Sordland, he wrote articles criticizing some of Leon Malenyev’s policies, arguing that Malenyevism was distorting the real ideals of Marcian socio-economics. He also heavily protested against the United Contanan Navy’s presence in Eastern Merkopa. He joined the PFJP as a social democrat in 1936 with hopes to enter the Grand National Assembly of Sordland, but he was denied top positions in the candidate lists due to his communist views, and couldn’t get elected.

In 1950, Stahler co-founded the CPS with a group of other socialist politicians and political theorists. He wrote a manifesto titled ‘Sordish Socialism,’ which caused a split within the party between the followers of Stahler’s ‘Sordish socialists’ and the Malenyevists. He invited the famous poet Bernard Circas to join the party ahead of their first elections in 1953, but was rejected.

In the ‘53 elections, he got just below 8% of the general vote, failing to pass the election threshold. After the election of President Rayne, he doubled his efforts to increase his party’s reach by opening new offices in every major city in Sordland.

After the elections of 1949, Kesaro was elected as the leader of the National Front and announced his bid for presidency. In the ‘53 elections, he managed to get the best results of NFP in its history, effectively becoming the third largest party in Sordland and the assembly.

In 1956, he was detained under charges of corruption.
